question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Y∼N(9,{12}^{2}),$ compute $P(Y\ge 17.76).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ |

$P(Y\ge 17.76)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =9$ and $\sigma =12.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 17.76) & =P(Z\ge \frac{17.76-9}{12}) \\  & =P\,(Z\ge \frac{8.76}{12}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.73)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/b41946733630a6c8a96b833f08d009d4df458af90cf196fab87e85bc35e83ca8.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.73) & =1-P(Z<0.73) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.73) \\  & =1-Φ(0.73)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.73)=0.7673.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.73) & =1-0.7673 \\  & =0.2327.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge 17.76)=0.2327.
$$
